translation_loss.what_was_lost: The literal meaning of 'Panchvati' as a grove of five sacred banyan/fig trees is lost in the generic translation 'The Grove of Panchvati'.
The specific cultural title 'Raghukulpati' (Lord of the Raghu clan) is translated as 'Lord of the Raghu clan', which loses the compact, compound Sanskritized poetic resonance of the original title.

The term 'satkar' literally means hospitality, welcoming, or honoring guests; translating 'vanya jeevan ka kiya satkar' as 'Embracing the wild with grace' shifts the active cultural practice of offering hospitality/respect to nature into a more passive emotional state of embracing it.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: Nature itself felt deeply moved, restless, or emotionally responsive to the profound love of Rama and Sita.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The wordplay on 'jad' (which means both 'root' of a plant/tree and 'inert/non-living matter' in philosophical contexts) in 'jad se jude' is simplified to 'rooted', losing the dual resonance of being connected to the physical earth/roots and the spiritual/material elements of nature.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The specific mythological and cosmological term 'Satyug' (the first and most righteous of the four cyclic cosmic ages in Hindu cosmology) is translated as 'the golden age', which replaces a precise cyclical Hindu temporal concept with a generic Western historical/literary trope.

original_poem:
पंचवटी

पर्णकुटी बनाकर वन में,  
माता सिया और रघुकुलपति,  
बसे पंचवटी के रमणीय क्षेत्र में,  
वन्य जीवन का किया सत्कार।

जड़ से जुड़े सहज स्नेह में,  
हरित छाया के उस आँगन में,  
राम का प्रेम स्नेहिल,  
वहाँ प्रकृति भी हुई विकल।

उस मिट्टी के कण-कण में,  
रामायण की गाथा गूँजी।  
पंचवटी के इस रमणीय क्षेत्र में,  
सतयुग की छवि पुनः पाई।
translated_poem:
The Grove of Panchvati

In a leafy hut in the woods,  
Lady Sita and the Lord of the Raghu clan,  
Settled in the lovely Panchvati grove,  
Embracing the wild with grace.

In the simple, rooted affection,  
In the courtyard of green shade,  
Rama’s love was tender and true,  
Even nature became restless there.

In each particle of that earth,  
Echoed the tale of the Ramayana.  
In this enchanting grove of Panchvati,  
The image of the golden age was revived again.
